mechanism_narrative: Positive GDP growth indicates a strong economy, leading to increased corporate earnings and thus higher S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive, but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in unemployment rate below 4% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE drops below 4%, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment and decline in unemployment indicates a robust economy, leading to higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Both PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% in a tightening cycle, but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong consumer demand, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts increase, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production above 105 indicates strong economic output, leading to higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO exceeds 105, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in GDP and housing starts indicates strong economic expansion, leading to higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Both GDPC1 and HOUST grow, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, low unemployment may not boost S&P 500 returns as much due to potential overheating.
failure_condition: UNRATE is below 4% in late-cycle, but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.
